merger_name: Triton - Bureau Veritas Fuel & Coal Testing, Inspection and Certification Division

anzsic_codes.name: Other Auxiliary Finance and Investment Services

merger_description:
Power BidCo Netherlands B.V., Power BidCo UK Limited and Power BidCo US LLC (together, the **Power BidCos**), each an indirectly wholly controlled special purpose vehicle of Triton Fund 6 GP SARL, propose to acquire 100% of each of IOL Investments B.V., Inspectorate International Ltd and Bureau Veritas Commodities & Trade Inc (together, the **Bureau Veritas Fuel & Coal Testing, Inspection and Certification Division**) from three subsidiaries of Bureau Veritas S.A., namely Bureau Veritas Nederland Holding B.V., Bureau Veritas Commodity Services Limited and Bureau Veritas Holdings Inc. (together, **Bureau Veritas**) (the **Acquisition**).

The Power BidCos are indirectly controlled by Triton Fund 6 GP SARL (**Triton Fund 6 GP**) in its capacity as general partner of Triton Fund 6 SCSp (which, together with a number of other limited partnerships, form part of Triton Fund 6). Triton Fund 6 is one of several investment funds (the **Triton Funds**) managed and advised by entities being part of the Triton group (collectively, **Triton**). The Triton Funds, including Triton Fund 6, are dedicated to investing in medium-sized companies headquartered in Central and Northern Europe, with a particular focus on three core sectors: Industrial Tech, Business Services, and Healthcare.

The target entities comprise Bureau Veritas' global Fuel & Coal Testing, Inspection and Certification division which operates across three principal product lines:

1. Oil & Petrochemicals (**O&P**), comprising O&P Trade, O&P Upstream and on-site/outsourced laboratory services;
2. Specialties, comprising Oil Condition Monitoring, Marine Fuels and Renewable Fuels; and
3. Coal, comprising Coal Upstream, Coal Downstream and Coal Trade.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition, given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between Triton (or its
connected entities) and the Bureau Veritas Fuel & Coal
Testing, Inspection and Certification Division in Australia
b. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
or conglomerate effects resulting from exclusionary
conduct, bundling or tying of products or services post-
acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
